layers.note: A low subshrub scattered through desert scrub, between the larger shrubs.

moisture.note: Dry, well-drained mesas, plains and sandy washes.

elevation_m.note: 100 to 2,100 m (Flora of North America); 2,000 to 5,000 feet in Arizona (Kearney and Peebles).

coldest_c.note: Across its range, coldest-month means from about 3 to 14 °C; gone below 0 °C and above 18 °C.

hard_freeze_c.note: Across its range, lows to about −11 °C borne, gone where the year's coldest night falls below about −15 °C.

warmest_c.note: Across its range, warmest-month means from about 25 to 34 °C; gone below 22 °C, where summers are too short, and above 37 °C.

degree_days_0.note: About 4,500 to 10,000 degree-days above 0 °C, none below 3,500.

degree_days_5.note: About 2,800 to 8,000 degree-days above 5 °C, none below 2,000.

moisture_index.note: A moisture index from about 0.04 to 0.3, gone by 0.02 and above 0.4.

summer_rain.note: No lower limit: it also grows where winter rain dominates, as in the Mojave Desert; where the monsoon brings summer rain, as on the bajada, up to about 0.7 of the year's precipitation in summer, gone by 0.8.

provenance.notes: Authored for the Saguaro desert scene (the west bajada of Saguaro National Park's Tucson Mountain District, about 750 m, 32.25 N 111.17 W) from general knowledge of the species and the ranges, habitats and elevations in the sources read for its spec (2026-10-19). Paperflower grows from southern Utah and Nevada to southern California, Arizona, Baja California and Sonora, in creosote-bush scrub and sandy washes (Flora of North America; Kearney and Peebles). Each climate range brackets the climate of that range, an approximate envelope read from these descriptions, not fitted to occurrence records; every full range holds the bajada's climate (coldest month about 11 °C, warmest about 31 °C, about 7,600 degree-days above 0 °C, coldest night about −4 °C, moisture index about 0.15, about half the year's rain in summer).
